rules.explanation: The build graph contains an x64 configuration that must be audited for ARM64 fallback or incomplete project mapping.
rules.recommendation: Add and verify an ARM64 mapping for every shipping and test project without removing the x64 baseline.

rules.explanation: An architecture-specific DIA SDK path selects x64 artifacts.
rules.recommendation: Resolve DIA library and runtime paths from the target platform and use the ARM64 SDK artifacts.

rules.explanation: The ARM64 toolchain probe trusts an architecture-named directory that may contain only ASAN payloads.
rules.recommendation: Require an ARM64 cl.exe and an ARM64 CRT library such as libcpmt.lib; do not accept directory existence.

rules.explanation: Visual Studio Installer exit 5007 indicates the modify operation was not elevated from process start.
rules.recommendation: Start an elevated shell first, rerun setup.exe modify, and retain the exact installer log and exit code.

rules.explanation: Visual Studio Installer exit 8006 indicates relevant Visual Studio or MSBuild processes were not fully quiesced.
rules.recommendation: Close Visual Studio and quiesce build, compiler-server, test, debugger, and installer processes before retrying.

rules.pattern: (?:BaseOutputPath/OutputPath property is not set|invalid combination of Configuration and Platform).*ARM64
rules.explanation: The solution selected ARM64 but at least one project has no usable ARM64 configuration/output mapping.
rules.recommendation: Add complete Debug/Release ARM64 project configurations, imports, output paths, and item definitions, then rerun PrepareForBuild across the full solution.

rules.pattern: project .* is not selected for building in solution configuration .*ARM64
rules.explanation: The ARM64 solution configuration silently skips a project, so the resulting app/test graph is incomplete.
rules.recommendation: Map every required shipping and test project to ARM64 and reject intentional exclusions unless the plan names and justifies them.

rules.explanation: Dependency restore and project compilation resolve different MSVC toolset versions, so headers, libraries, and compiler built-ins are inconsistent.
rules.recommendation: Pin one installed VCToolsVersion for vcpkg and MSBuild, clear stale environment paths, and assert the resolved cl/link paths and versions before building.

rules.explanation: A legacy v142 ARM64 compiler is paired with a current Windows SDK, an unverified combination that can fail inside SDK headers.
rules.recommendation: Use a coherent current ARM64 toolset/SDK pair or explicitly install and validate a compatible older SDK; do not inherit legacy toolsets accidentally.

rules.explanation: The compiler and linker/library search paths resolve different MSVC installations, indicating stale LIB/PATH leakage.
rules.recommendation: Start from a clean developer environment, remove stale PATH/LIB/INCLUDE entries, and assert one toolset root for cl.exe, link.exe, headers, and ARM64 libraries.

rules.explanation: A CI step is allowed to fail without failing the job; when used for build, test, purity, or package gates this can publish a false green result.
rules.recommendation: Remove continue-on-error from hard gates, or add a mandatory final step that parses retained results and exits nonzero for any failed suite/check.

rules.explanation: A source file carries non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes without a UTF-8 BOM, so MSVC decodes it with the active code page and silently corrupts identifiers, literals, and include paths.
rules.recommendation: Add a UTF-8 BOM to the re-encoded file; never normalize upstream ANSI sources to BOM-less UTF-8 during a port, and do not reach for project-wide /utf-8 when the tree holds legitimate Windows-1252 fixtures.

rules.pattern: error C1083: Cannot open include file: '[^']*\u00C3[^']*'
rules.explanation: A missing include name contains mojibake, proving the compiler decoded the source with the wrong code page rather than the encoding it was saved in.
rules.recommendation: Fix the source encoding instead of renaming fixtures or deleting the non-ASCII test data, then re-run the build on every target platform.

rules.explanation: One target architecture was compiled by more than one MSVC host toolchain flavour in a single build, so the host that produced the binaries is not reproducible and is not the pinned one.
rules.recommendation: Pin PreferredToolArchitecture, resolve the matching MSBuild host binary, and assert the host directory of every cl.exe/link.exe invocation parsed out of the retained build log rather than a preflight probe.

rules.explanation: The GitHub contents API transcodes file content, so its payload cannot support a byte-level claim. Measured on one real file it reported size 19184 while its own base64 decoded to 19187 bytes, and it rendered a Windows-1252 source identically to a broken UTF-8 one, which caused a published root-cause analysis to be wrong.
rules.recommendation: Compare git blob ids from the trees API, or fetch /git/blobs and recompute the object id from the payload, whenever the claim is about bytes, encoding, or file identity.

rules.explanation: PowerShell redirection and Out-File route through the output encoding, so raw git object bytes are decoded and re-encoded on the way to disk. The resulting file is not the blob, which silently corrupts any encoding or hash comparison performed against it.
rules.recommendation: Pipe to Set-Content -AsByteStream, or capture the bytes and write them with [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes, so the blob reaches disk unmodified.

rules.explanation: The build pins PreferredToolArchitecture but never proves which compiler MSBuild invoked. Microsoft.Cpp.ToolsetLocation.props declares that property TreatAsLocalProperty, so imported props may reassign a value supplied on the command line, and a preflight that probes a compiler reports the one that resolves rather than the one that runs. Two runs of the same project on the same runner label, both passing the pin, compiled under different host toolchains.
rules.recommendation: After each build, parse the cl.exe and link.exe command lines out of the retained build log and fail on an unexpected host directory, on mixed toolset versions, or on zero invocations. Treat the log parse as the authority and the pin as an unverified request.
